• **Best for sightseeing:** October – April. Mild, sunny days (20–28°C), perfect for the Pyramids and Luxor temples. December–January are coolest but busiest.
• **Best for Red Sea beaches:** May – September. Warm sea, crystal-clear water, ideal for Hurghada and Sharm El-Sheikh diving. Inland cities get very hot (40°C+).
• **Shoulder months (fewer crowds):** March–April and October–November. Pleasant weather and lower prices.

🛂 **Visa & Entry Requirements**

Most visitors need a visa to enter Egypt. The easiest options:
• **E-visa (recommended):** Apply online at visa2egypt.gov.eg at least 7 days before travel. Single-entry from $30 USD; multiple-entry from $65 USD. Valid for stays up to 3 months.
• **Visa on arrival:** Available at approved kiosks in the arrival hall. Around $25–36 USD, payable in cash. Valid for 30 days.
• **Free Sinai stamp:** If you fly directly to Sharm El-Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba or Taba and stay only in South Sinai for up to 15 days, you get a free entry stamp. You cannot leave the Sinai region on this stamp.

**Passport rule:** Must be valid for at least 6 months from your arrival date.

🩺 **Safety & Health**

• **Tap water:** Do NOT drink it. Stick to sealed bottled water, even for brushing teeth.
• **Vaccines (UK travellers):** Hepatitis A and Typhoid are recommended. Hepatitis B for some. Rabies for longer stays. Malaria tablets are not needed for standard tourist routes. Book a travel health appointment 6–8 weeks before departure.
• **Scams to avoid:** Ignore unsolicited 'gifts' or 'free' camel rides around the Pyramids. Agree prices in advance for horse carriages, boats and taxis. Only use licensed guides and reputable dive operators.
• **Emergency numbers:** Police 122 · Tourist Police 126 · Ambulance 123.
• **Travel insurance:** Essential. Consider medical evacuation cover — treatment for serious incidents may not be available locally.
